name: trend_strength_adaptive_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, the strength of an intraday trend (measured by 3-minute ADX) determines how fast directional momentum can be captured: high-ADX regimes (ADX > 35) reflect concentrated institutional order flow where even a 30-second window is sufficient to confirm direction, while low-ADX regimes (ADX 18-25) require 2-3 minutes of EMA history to filter noise. The adaptive EMA crossover exploits this by contracting its lookback from ~36 bars (3 min) to ~12 bars (1 min) as ADX rises, making the signal faster precisely when fast signals are reliable. The +DI/-DI comparison on 3-minute bars confirms that directional pressure is asymmetric — not just overall volatility — while the VWAP filter ensures the trade aligns with the accumulated session-level institutional flow benchmarking on NIFTY.

indicators.name: adx_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute ADX (36 bars × 5s = 180s) as the regime-scaling parameter. Compressed from original's 14-min ADX because we're holding 15-120s — we need trend strength that reflects the CURRENT minute, not the past 14. At 5s bars, the 3-min ADX is fast enough to distinguish a trending micro-burst from a choppy range, which is exactly the regime information needed to adapt the EMA lookback.

indicators.name: plus_di_36
indicators.purpose: Bullish directional index on 3-minute window. Confirms that up-moves are systematically larger than down-moves in the current micro-trend, not just total volatility rising.

indicators.name: minus_di_36
indicators.purpose: Bearish directional index on same 3-minute window. Used with +DI to determine directional asymmetry.

indicators.name: adaptive_ema_fast
indicators.purpose: Fast EMA whose alpha contracts as ADX rises. At ADX=15: lookback≈43 bars (3.6 min); ADX=30: 38 bars (3.2 min); ADX=60: 28 bars (2.3 min); ADX=100: 12 bars (1 min). Range 12-48 vs original 5-25 bars (1-min): compressed because 5s bars resolve micro-moves that 1-min bars average away. The adaptive contraction captures acceleration in the signal exactly when acceleration is meaningful — during strong NIFTY momentum pulses.

indicators.name: adaptive_ema_slow
indicators.purpose: Slow EMA = 2× fast EMA lookback, providing the crossover reference. Same adaptive logic: at high ADX, slow becomes more responsive but still 2× slower than fast, maintaining signal quality.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.formula: cumulative sum(typical_price * volume) / cumulative sum(volume) from 09:15 IST, reset each day
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP — no scaling needed, cumulative. Filters directional bias: NIFTY above VWAP means institutional buyside flow has dominated the session; entering CE there aligns with accumulated demand. Below VWAP: net sell pressure has dominated. Directional accuracy improves significantly when entry aligns with VWAP-side bias.

conditions: ADX(36)[t] > ADX(36)[t-6] (ADX rising over 30s = trend is accelerating)
adaptive_ema_fast > adaptive_ema_slow — adaptive EMA crossover bullish
close > VWAP — aligned with session institutional buy flow
adaptive_ema_fast < adaptive_ema_slow — adaptive EMA crossover bearish
close < VWAP — aligned with session institutional sell flow

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option pts = ~8 NIFTY spot pts at delta 0.5. For a 3-minute ADX trend, an 8-spot-pt adverse move within the 15-120s hold means the institutional order creating the trend has paused or reversed — thesis is broken. NIFTY 30s typical range is 2-5 option pts; 4 pts gives one full 30s range of room before invalidating the setup.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option pts = ~14 NIFTY spot pts. ADX-confirmed trending moves on NIFTY extend 15-25 spot pts in the first 60-90 seconds; targeting 14 pts captures ~60% of the typical first leg. 1:1.75 R:R, above the ~1.5 required for the 55% win rate threshold to be profitable.

filters.vix_filter: none — strategy works across VIX regimes; ADX captures trend quality independent of absolute volatility level
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:20 (ADX warmup: 2×36 = 72 bars = 6 min) or after 15:25
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY index volume noisy at 5s; directional pressure captured by DI indicators
filters.trend_filter: ADX > 18 AND DI asymmetry — dual condition prevents entries in choppy regimes
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at candle close

edge.edge_decay_risk: Moderate — ADX-adaptive parameter scaling is a novel twist on standard ADX trend-following; the adaptive EMA contraction adds complexity that most participants don't implement

adaptation_notes: Original traded ADX(14) on 1-min bars of NIFTY50 stocks with 15-60 min holds. KEY CHANGES: (1) ADX compressed from 14 min to 3 min (ADX(36) at 5s bars) — proportional to hold time reduction from 15-60 min to 15-120s. (2) Adaptive EMA formula re-calibrated: original used max(5, 25-floor(ADX/5)) bars on 1-min = range 5-25 min; converted to max(12, 48-floor(ADX/3)) at 5s = range 60-240s, targeting the same proportional effect. (3) ADX-rising check expanded from 3 bars (3 min original) to 6 bars (30s at 5s) — catches acceleration at our timescale. (4) Stock-specific filters removed (ADV, earnings, bid-ask spread <5bps). (5) Fixed ₹1L capital per pipeline conventions instead of ADX-proportional sizing. DIFFERENTIATOR vs adx_trend_strength_v1: that strategy uses fixed ADX(60) with DI-spread threshold; this strategy uses ADX-ADAPTIVE EMA crossover as primary signal — fundamentally different entry logic.
weaknesses: Adaptive EMA alpha changes bar-by-bar as ADX fluctuates, potentially generating false crossovers when ADX crosses the boundary that shifts lookback — same weakness as original, amplified at 5s frequency due to noisier ADX readings
ADX(36) on 5s NIFTY bars is very short (3 minutes); ADX may oscillate rapidly, causing frequent lookback changes that destabilize EMA convergence
All 5 entry conditions creating a tight conjunction reduces trade frequency; in low-ADX sessions NIFTY may generate 0-2 trades/day
